principle: Build every asset as measured parts made from the technical drawing; tessellate each part to the user's fidelity. Never build one dense voxel surface and simplify it.

rules.rule: No geometry selected from an object name; no rule tuned to one example. Every rule is geometric or measured and stated in its docstring.
The drawing stage runs first and is identical for every fidelity. Nothing builds from raw painted outlines.
Every new step sits behind a switch; the current pipeline keeps building every object until the new path beats it on the same inputs.
Gate for every change: before/after contact sheet on the drawn regression set and the seven image-only objects; any asset worse = not done.
QA thresholds are never loosened to make something pass.
No new Blender dependencies. New code is plain Python (numpy, scipy, build123d/OpenCascade, trimesh, xatlas). Blender stays default behind HULL_BACKEND=blender|python until parity.
No bug-fix loops: one hypothesis = one change = one test; stop at the order's attempt limit, revert uncommitted work, write a report.
Never kill processes by image name; stop only processes you started, by PID.

Same photo, same mesh: a build is a pure function of input image, order and code version; repeat builds give byte-identical GLBs. Nothing a previous build wrote (learning memory, caches, .hull-runs) may change geometry. reconstruction_memory_mode defaults to off; learning is experiment-only and reports reproducible: false. A repeat-build difference is a defect, never a tolerance. Scope: same input, order, code and toolchain (Blender version, Python packages, OS); after a toolchain change rebuild baselines once, compare old vs new by measurement, record it, then require byte identity again.

QA at the profile tolerance: a drawing view passes when its p95 outline distance <= max(2t, floor), floor = max(1 mm, 2 QA raster px, 1.5 x sheet mm per source px); size within max(3t, floor); IoU reported, backstop fail below 0.80 only; t below the floor -> unverifiable at this fidelity (reported, never a pass); mesh-health limits independent of t.

pipeline.name: drawing
steps: orient plan views (8 orientations scored against front/side)
reconcile opposite views (keep a one-view part if the other two directions support it)

pipeline.name: tessellate_per_part
pipeline.out: game or engineering mesh, parts welded at seams

pipeline.name: texture_and_bake
pipeline.status: existing in Blender; python port planned (Codex Order 9)

fallback.when: per part, when its sections do not fit lines, arcs and superellipses within tolerance (organic: sofa cushion, carved leg)

Part.name: str (unique)
Part.profiles: drawing profile references per view (vertices_px with bulges)
Part.sections: list of stations [along, a0, a1, b0, b1] normalised, with superellipse exponent n per axis
Part.features: list of {kind: bump|hole|boss, axis, edge, along, cut, keep, measured_in}
Part.attachment: {parent: part name | null, contact: face/axis, offset_mm}
Part.paint_ownership: per view: pixel mask of this part
Part.detail_maps: markings/grilles/numerals as texture and normal-map sources (never carved)
Part.evidence: views and detail views supporting this part; accepted only if >= 2 views agree

sources: drawing: abrupt section changes split parts (rounding.tracks ratio 0.8)
part graph (part_graph.py) matching detail views, later

fidelity.game_tolerance: t = distance_m * pixel_angle; pixel_angle = 2*tan(fov_deg/2)/lines, default fov_deg 60, lines 1080 -> 0.00097 rad

tessellation.feature_to_texture: a feature standing out from its part by less than t, or narrower than 2t, becomes albedo + normal map only
tessellation.seams: parts welded; no simplification of a whole-object mesh
tessellation.shading: smooth across each exact (B-rep) face of a part; hard edges at B-rep edges whose faces meet at more than 30 degrees, at part seams and around features. Never a fixed angle between mesh facets (a 7-sided handle has 51 degrees between facets and must still read round).

checks.method: six orthographic ray-cast silhouettes stretched with painted outlines to one box
triangles projected along each axis at 0.5 mm/px vs drawn profile, no rescaling
checks.limit: aligned at mesh bbox corner (Codex Order 3 registers on main body)

checks.method: mesh rotated over azimuth (15 deg) and elevation (5-60 deg, from above), refined, fitted to picture outline box
z-buffer at solved pose; least squares brightness = n . l + c from mesh normals

migration.name: tessellate per part + bake from part model
retire voxel path for manufactured parts; keep as organic fallback
